info.title: work API
info.description: Served by the backend and consumed by the frontend through orval. Reached through the frontend's /api/v1 proxy.

requestBody.description: PNG, JPEG, WebP, ICO or a plain SVG, at most 256 KB

post.summary:
Second step of a sign-in. A challenge allows 5 tries; every miss also counts toward the
account lock-out.
Single-use, expiring token. Every session of the account is revoked afterwards.

Always answers `200`, whether or not the address belongs to an account, so it cannot be used to
find out who is registered. At most 3 mails per address and hour.

Rotating refresh tokens. Presenting an already-used token means it leaked (or was
replayed), so the whole token family is revoked.

With e-mail verification on (the default whenever SMTP is configured), this never creates an
account and never says whether the address is taken: it stores a pending registration and mails
a link, or, for a known address, mails a notice. Without SMTP the account is created at once
and a taken address answers `409`.

get.summary:
Redirects the browser to the provider. `provider` is `google`, `github`, `microsoft`, `slack`
or `saml`, as far as the instance configured it.

post.summary: Turns a pending registration into an account and signs the new user in. The link works once.

Creates (or rotates) the secret URL of an automation with the `webhook` trigger. The previous
URL stops working immediately. Only a hash of the secret is stored.

get.summary:
What every visitor sees: the instance's name, description, accent colour and whether it has its
own favicon. Public on purpose (the sign-in page needs it).

Updates of the other editors as server-sent events: `{"t":"update","u":<base64>,"from":<user>}`,
and `{"t":"reset"}` when the field was changed outside the editor.

post.summary: Pushes local changes and pulls the ones the client lacks.

get.summary:
Server-sent events for the caller's own notifications. The stream is bound to the user id in
the verified token; clients cannot name or join any other channel.

post.summary:
Public endpoint: the secret in the URL is the credential. Unknown id, wrong secret, disabled and
deleted automations all look the same (404). The run happens in the background.

requestBody.description: Any JSON object. Available as {{trigger.body.*}}; include `card_id` to act on an issue.

get.summary:
Open an issue by its key alone (`ACME-12`), like Jira's /browse/KEY-12. Malformed keys,
unknown keys and issues the caller may not see are all the same 404.

post.summary:
Invites to a single list: whoever accepts becomes a limited-access member of the project (or
keeps their membership) and is granted `role` on this list only.

Like the project invitation, but for one list: the invited address becomes a limited-access
member that only sees this list (existing members just get access to it).

delete.summary:
Deletes the account. Refused while the user is the only owner of a project that other people
still use: transfer or delete the project first.

patch.summary:
Only these two fields are editable here. Email changes would need re-verification and roles are
never client-writable.

get.summary: Managing tokens needs a real session, so a leaked token cannot mint more tokens.

post.summary: Both factors are needed to switch MFA off again.
Confirms enrolment with a code from the authenticator and returns the recovery codes.
Replaces all recovery codes with a fresh set.

Starts enrolment: stores a fresh pending secret (replacing an unconfirmed one). MFA is only
active once `/me/mfa/enable` has seen a valid code.

Requires the current password. Every other session is revoked, so a leaked token or cookie
stops working the moment the password changes.

get.summary:
The caller's live sign-ins, most recently active first. Needs a real session, so an API
token cannot enumerate them.

delete.summary: "Sign out everywhere else": every sign-in except the one making the request.

Signs out one device. Its access token stops working immediately because the session is
re-checked on every request.
Disconnects a provider, unless it is the only way left to sign in.

post.summary: Starts connecting a provider to the signed-in account. Needs a real session.

get.summary: Always scoped to the caller: there is no way to ask for another user's notifications.

post.summary: Mails an invitation that only the invited address can redeem (the account's e-mail must match).

patch.summary:
Rule: you can only manage members ranked strictly below you, and only grant roles
strictly below your own. Ownership is never granted or removed through this API.

get.summary: Public, non-sensitive facts the sign-in pages need.

Look a workspace up by its issue-key prefix (`ACME`), case-insensitively. Unknown keys and
workspaces of projects the caller is not in look identical.
Open an issue by its key (`WORK-12`), like Jira's /browse/KEY-12.
"Your work": issues of this workspace assigned to the caller, newest activity first.
Spaces and lists of a workspace that the caller is allowed to see.

workspace_id.description: Set for list invites, so the client can open the list afterwards.

mentions.description: Users to notify, for comments. Only members of the project are notified.

type.description: `comment`, `email`, `task`, `call`, `message` or `meeting` (`update` entries are written by the system)

token.description: The secret. It is not stored and cannot be shown again.

token_prefix.description: First characters of the token, to recognise it. The full token is shown only once.

AuthOut.description:
Result of a sign-in or sign-up step. Exactly one of three shapes: a session
(`access_token`), a second step (`mfa_required` + `mfa_token`) or a pending confirmation
(`verification_required`).

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

mfa_required.description: The password was right, but a code from the authenticator (or a recovery code) is needed.

mfa_token.description: Present with `mfa_required`: send it with the code to `/auth/mfa/verify`. Valid for 5 minutes.

verification_required.description:
A confirmation e-mail was sent. The answer is the same whether or not the address is
already registered.

has_webhook.description: A webhook URL exists for this automation (trigger type `webhook`).

accent.description: `#RRGGBB`; the interface derives its accent colour from it.

version.description: Changes whenever the branding does, so caches can be bypassed.

order.description: Position within the stage (lower first). Defaults to the end.

options.description: Pass to `navigator.credentials.create()` / `.get()` as `publicKey` (binary values are base64url).

move_to.description: Where unfinished issues go: another sprint of this list, or `null` for the backlog.

card_type_id.description: Defaults to the list's default card type.

stage_id.description: Defaults to the first stage of the list.

expires_in_days.description: 1-365 days; omit for a token that never expires.

FieldPatch.description: Slug and type are immutable: card data is keyed by slug and validated by type.

url.description: Same-origin download URL (requires the Authorization header).

config_keys.description: JSON keys the step expects in `config`.

enabled.description: Integrations this instance has configured. Others cannot be connected.

token.description: Shown exactly once; only its hash is stored.

url.description: Open this address to connect the provider.

role.description: The caller's effective role on this list: `viewer`, `member`, `admin` or `owner`.

auth_method.description: How this request was authenticated: `session` or `api_token`.

mfa_enabled.description: Two-factor authentication is switched on for this account.

restricted.description: Limited access: sees only the lists and spaces they were explicitly added to.

otpauth_uri.description: `otpauth://` URI; render it as a QR code.

code.description: Code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code.

config.description: Settings that matter for running the instance. Never contains a secret.

recovery_codes.description: Shown once. Each code works one time.

name.description: A name to tell the passkeys apart ("Laptop", "Phone").

password.description: Required for accounts that have a password.

restricted.description: Limit the member to the lists and spaces they hold a grant on. Needs the role `viewer`.

role.description: New project role. Granting `member` or higher ends limited access.

filters.description: Filter tree, see the filter documentation: `{"and":[{"field":"data.title","operator":"like","value":"x"}]}`

keyword.description: Case-insensitive match on the issue title or key (`WORK-12`).

sprint.description: Scrum lists: `backlog` (not in any sprint), `active` (the running sprint) or a sprint id.

SessionOut.description:
One sign-in. Refresh tokens rotate, so a sign-in is a token family: it is identified by the
family id, which stays the same for as long as the sign-in lives.

current.description: This is the session making the request.

user_agent.description: Browser / device, as reported when the session was last used.

secret.description: Hex key. Outbound webhooks carry `X-Work-Signature: sha256=HMAC_SHA256(key, raw body)`.

sprint_id.description: Target sprint, or `null` to move the issue back to the backlog.

points.description: Sum of the `story_points` field over the sprint's issues.

action_type.description: One of the action types from the catalog.

seed.description: Base64 initial document, used only if no session document exists yet (needs write access).

state_vector.description: Base64 state vector of the client's document, so the answer only holds what it lacks.

update.description: Base64 Yjs update with local changes (needs write access).

empty.description: No session document exists yet and none was seeded: the caller should seed it.

state_vector.description: Base64 state vector of the server's document.

update.description: Base64 update with everything the client lacks.

email_verification_required.description: Sign-up needs a confirmed e-mail address.

mail_enabled.description: Outgoing e-mail is configured (password reset, invitations, notifications by e-mail).

passkeys_available.description: Passkeys can be used (they need the page to be served over https, or localhost).

sso_oidc_name.description: Label for the `oidc` provider, e.g. the name of the company's identity provider.

sso_providers.description:
Single sign-on providers configured on this instance (`google`, `github`, `microsoft`,
`slack`, `saml`).

expires_in.description:
Seconds until the access token expires. The refresh token is never in the body:
it is set as an HttpOnly cookie so scripts (and XSS) cannot read it.

collab_keep.description:
Rich-text fields this save belongs to a live collaborative editing session of the caller.
Writes to any other rich field end the field's session; see `collab.rs`.

data.description: Merge patch: keys are set, `null` clears a key. Unknown keys are rejected.

disabled.description: Blocks sign-in everywhere (sessions end at once) or lifts the block.

unlock.description: Clears a lock-out after failed sign-ins.

path.description: Path to POST to, relative to the site origin. It contains the secret and is shown only once.

key_prefix.description: Optional issue key prefix; derived from the name when omitted.
Prefix of issue keys, e.g. `WORK` for `WORK-12`.
